summary: A selective review of recent submissions finds one physics-calibrated generative neutrino model and one flow-based lattice-QCD sampler as the strongest AI/ML-relevant results. Heavy-ion relevance is concentrated in nPDF uncertainty practice and a controlled tensor-network study of string fragmentation; neither should be overread as a direct heavy-ion measurement.
strongest_paper_summary: Experimental calibration of an event-level neutrino-nucleus generative surrogate with cross-observable and cross-flux checks.

papers.short_authors: J. L. Bonilla et al. (6 authors)
papers.abstract: Generative surrogate for charged-current nu_mu-nucleus scattering calibrated to MicroBooNE differential cross sections; improves held-out observables and transfers across fluxes without retuning.

papers.title: Ergodic topology sampling toward the continuum with Stochastic Normalizing Flows
papers.abstract: Combines open boundaries and stochastic normalizing flows to control topological freezing in SU(3) Yang-Mills down to 0.03 fm.

papers.title: Nuclear PDFs
papers.abstract: LHCP2026 status contribution on global nPDF analyses, uncertainty calibration, and the need to treat A-dependence more carefully in the LHC nuclei-collision era.

papers.title: Collective Organization of String Fragmentation
papers.short_authors: R. A. Janik et al. (4 authors)
